rationale: A wins because it keeps the story shapes clean and knows which claims would get the founder slapped by a competent reporter. “A canned-water brand says it has given $4.2M to clean-water charities. Here's what that buys.” is a real accountability angle with real proof demands. B has useful bones, but “Liquid Death's new store sells water you can't buy anywhere else — for now” invents exclusivity and future-distribution suspense from a fact pattern that only says limited-edition canned water. That is not strategy; that is garnish wearing a press badge.
gaps_in_A: “Liquid Death opens a store that sells almost no water” overstates the supplied facts. The update says the store sells merch, limited-edition canned water, and runs events; it does not prove water is marginal in the product mix.
“The standard just got a stress test” is a strong frame, but the sustainability tension is an inference. It needs B Corp score, criteria, and outside standards context before anyone pitches it hard.
“Weak on its own” is accurate for the donation angle, but it also admits the hole: the $4.2M figure is context unless tied tightly to the B Corp certification or verified recipient outcomes.
gaps_in_B: “Liquid Death says it's profitable. It just won't say by how much.” is the dangerous swap. The update says contribution-margin profitable with net profit undisclosed; calling that “profitable” is exactly the kind of slippage a finance reporter will punish.

“store sells water you can't buy anywhere else — for now” and “store-exclusive can” invent exclusivity and suspense. The facts only say limited-edition canned water, and explicitly say no new product line was announced.
“near-total retail penetration” overclaims the 120,000-door fact. Large footprint, yes; near-total requires a denominator B does not have.

The ESG angle mushes two sharper stories together: “A $4.2M clean-water tally and a new B Corp badge” is serviceable, but it loses A’s cleaner separation between donation-accountability and certification-standards stories.
